questions.question: Explain why the divorce rate has increased in the UK since the 1960s.

points.text: Divorce increased because: (1) legal changes - 1969 Divorce Reform Act made divorce easier; (2) secularisation - less religious opposition; (3) less stigma - divorce is now socially acceptable; (4) women's economic independence - women can afford to leave unhappy marriages; (5) rising expectations - Giddens' confluent love means people expect personal fulfilment; (6) media normalisation - divorce

points.text: Key changes: falling birth rate (1.6 children per woman, below replacement), rising life expectancy (81 years), ageing population (19% over 65), declining marriage, rising cohabitation and divorce. points.text: New Right: yes - declining marriage causes family breakdown, fatherless families, and social problems.
